title: He Rang About His Name Badge

scenes.text: HE LOST HIS BADGE. IT HAS MY NAME.
scenes.narration: A man phoned the lost property office to ask if anyone had handed in his name badge. He read me the name on it. It was mine.
scenes.imagePrompt: An old beige desk telephone with a coiled cord on a cluttered desk under a lamp, the receiver lifted off its cradle, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain

scenes.narration: I am wearing my badge. I looked down to check while he was talking.
scenes.imagePrompt: A plastic staff badge clipped to a grey cardigan, the photo on it blurred, seen from above as if looking down at one's own chest, no face visible, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain

scenes.narration: He asked me to look on the third shelf, behind the umbrellas. There was a badge there. Same name. Same photo.
scenes.imagePrompt: Behind a row of tagged black umbrellas on a steel shelf, a small plastic staff badge lying face down, lit through wire mesh, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain

scenes.narration: I asked when he would collect it. He said he works nights. Then he said thank you, in my voice, and put the phone down.
